issues.legal_issue: An ordinary lessee who holds land under its owner and is liable to pay rent is a tenant, not a landowner entitled to seek ejectment of another tenant on the ground of personal cultivation.
material_facts: The appellant held a lease from the owner over a larger area that included the land occupied by the respondent as a tenant-at-will.
The appellant sought the respondent’s ejectment for the appellant’s own cultivation, claiming to be a small landowner.
The appellant was not an allottee or lessee within the special categories included by the governing definition of landowner, and was not a mortgagee in possession.
The appellant held the land under the owner and was liable to pay rent for it.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was a tenant rather than a landowner and was not entitled to eject the respondent; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(1) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, “landowner” takes its meaning from section 3(2) of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887, subject to specified inclusions for certain allot tees and lessees and for a mortgagee in possession. Section 3(2) excludes a tenant from the definition of landowner. Under section 4(5) of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, a person who holds land under another and is liable to pay rent for it is a tenant, unless an enumerated exception applies. An ordinary lessee satisfying that definition is therefore excluded from being a landowner under the relevant definitions and cannot claim the landowner’s right to eject. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.ejectment_application_by_intermediate_le: A person who leases land from an owner applies to eject another tenant occupying part of that leased land.
predicates.claimant_holds_land_under_owner: The claimant holds the land under another person who owns it.
predicates.claimant_is_liable_to_pay_rent: The claimant is liable to pay the owner rent for the land held under that owner.
predicates.claimant_falls_within_no_tenant_exceptio: The claimant does not fall within an exception to the ordinary tenant definition or a specially included landowner category.
predicates.lessee_cannot_eject_tenant_as_landowner: The claimant cannot eject the occupying tenant by relying on rights available to a landowner.

issues.definition: When an intermediate lessee applies to eject a tenant, holds the land under an owner, owes rent, and falls within neither a tenant exception nor a special landowner category, the lessee cannot eject the tenant as a landowner.
